q: 1. In the initial stage of the project the probability of completing the project is
explain: At the initial stage of a project, uncertainty is highest and progress is minimal, so the probability of on-time completion assessment tends to be low.

q: 2. The process of incorporating changes and rescheduling or replanning is called
explain: Updating is the process of incorporating changes and rescheduling/replanning the project based on actual progress.

q: 3. The constraints in case of resource smoothening operation would be
options: both resources and project duration time
explain: In resource smoothening, the project duration is kept fixed (as the constraint) while resource allocation is adjusted within non-critical activities' float.

q: 4. The independent float affects only
explain: Independent float pertains solely to the specific activity in question, without any bearing on preceding or succeeding activities.

q: 5. An event is:
options: a definite position of an activity
explain: An event represents the terminal points (start or end nodes) of an activity in a network diagram.

q: 6. Choose the correct statement from the following:
explain: PERT is indeed event-oriented, making this the correct statement among the options.

q: 7. Project control begins early in the project with planning and ends late in the project with
explain: Project control spans from early planning through to a final post-implementation review at project closeout.

q: 8. The time by which activity completion time can be delayed without affecting the start of succeeding activities is known as:
explain: Free float specifically defines the permissible delay in an activity that does not affect the succeeding activity's start time.

q: 9. If the scheduled completion time of a project is more than the earliest expected time for completion of the project, then the probability of completion of the project within the scheduled completion time will be
explain: If the scheduled time exceeds the expected (mean) time, the project has a higher-than-average chance of completion within schedule, i.e., more than 50%.

q: 10. Aggregate planning is planning for
explain: Aggregate planning looks at the total capacity and resource needs for the entire project rather than individual small tasks.

q: 11. Critical path moves along the activities having total float?
explain: By definition, the critical path consists of activities with zero total float.

q: 12. The objective of technical planning is
options: initiating the procurement action of resources
taking remedial action about bottle-neck in execution
explain: Technical planning covers the entire lifecycle from setting standards to resource management and problem-solving during execution.

q: 13. For the execution of work in time, work plan is prepared by
explain: The contractor is responsible for creating the detailed schedule and work plan to ensure they meet the contractual deadlines.

q: 14. Which one is the basis of project?
explain: A project is built on the pillars of planning what to do, scheduling when to do it, and monitoring to ensure it is done correctly.

q: 15. In PERT (Programme Evaluation & Review Technique) analysis the duration of the activities is taken as:
explain: PERT uses the expected mean time (calculated from the three time estimates) as the duration for scheduling calculations.

q: 16. The total float for any activity along the critical path in CPM is:
explain: Activities on the critical path always have zero total float, by definition.

q: 17. Critical path method (CPM) requires:
explain: CPM uses a single deterministic time estimate for each activity, unlike PERT's three estimates.

q: 18. CPM stand for:
explain: CPM stands for Critical Path Method.

q: 19. A bar chart is drawn for:
explain: A bar chart plots time against activities, with bar length representing each activity's duration.

q: 20. A CPM network is updated
options: whenever there is differences in the planned and actual performance
explain: Network updating is done whenever a deviation is found between planned and actual performance, requiring revision.

q: 21. In PERT, optimistic time represents the following time taken by an activity.
options: expected or average time taken when the activity is repeated several times
time taken if there is delay at every stage except due to natural calamities
minimum possible time taken under ideal conditions
most likely time taken under normal conditions
explain: Optimistic time represents the minimum possible duration an activity would take assuming everything goes ideally well.

q: 22. PERT stands for
options: Pertinent equation related to a task
explain: PERT stands for Programme Evaluation and Review Technique.

q: 23. Completion of an activity on CPM network diagram, is generally known
explain: Completion of an activity is marked by an event, represented as a node/connector point - all of above apply.

q: 24. Latest finish time CPM technique is indicated by a:
explain: In many CPM notations, latest finish time is indicated in a rectangular box associated with the node.

q: 25. Negative slack occurs:
options: When latest allowable time is greater than earliest expected time
When events stick to their schedule
explain: Negative slack typically results from a deficiency of resources causing schedule delays beyond the allowable time.

q: 26. Float may be defined as the difference between
options: latest start time and the earliest start time
latest finish time and the earliest finish time
time available and time required to complete the activity
explain: Float can be equivalently expressed via any of these differences (LST-EST, LFT-EFT, or available-required time) - all of the above are valid definitions.

q: 27. For completion of a project, the critical path of the network represents:
explain: The critical path represents the minimum time required to complete the entire project.

q: 28. Gantt chart is drawn for
explain: A Gantt chart plots activities against time, similar to a standard bar chart.

q: 29. PERT technique of network analysis is mainly useful for:
explain: BUT AS PER BOOK C .PERT is a scheduling/planning technique, not related to tender inviting, opening, or awarding processes - hence none of the above.

q: 30. When float or slack of an activity is positive, it represents
explain: Positive float indicates spare time is available for the activity, implying flexibility/availability of extra time (and by extension resources) without impacting overall completion.

q: 31. The pictorial representation of activities and events of a project is called
explain: The network diagram is the standard pictorial representation depicting a project's activities and events with their interrelationships.

q: 32. The object of technical planning, is
options: initiating the procurement action of resources
explain: Technical planning covers preparing specifications, estimates, and initiating resource procurement - all of the above.

q: 33. Inputs used during scope planning include all of the following except
explain: Scope planning inputs typically include the project charter, product description, and constraints, but detailed budget/cost analysis is not a direct input to scope planning.

q: 34. A project has three independent critical paths A, B and C. To reduce the project length, we have to shorten
options: The activities of A, B and C
explain: When multiple independent critical paths exist, shortening the project duration requires reducing activities on all of them simultaneously (A, B, and C).
